text:
## Description

Determine whether every unpainted cell can be painted black or white so that the final black cells occupy exactly one nonempty, axis-aligned rectangle. The Python 3 program reads the grid from standard input and prints the decision to standard output.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** — The first input line contains integers `H` and `W`, each between 1 and 1000 inclusive.
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** — The next `H` lines describe the rows from top to bottom. Each line contains exactly `W` characters from `#`, `.`, and `?`, representing black, white, and unpainted cells, respectively.
- **PRE-3 (Unverified)** — At least one cell is already black.

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** — The program prints exactly one answer line. It prints `Yes` if at least one valid completion exists and `No` otherwise.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** — A valid completion assigns black or white to every `?` cell and preserves every existing `#` and `.` cell. All cells inside one rectangle are black, and all cells outside it are white.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** — The rectangle spans consecutive rows and consecutive columns within the grid. A single cell, a single row or column segment, and the entire grid are valid rectangle shapes. Multiple valid completions still produce a single `Yes`.

## Test suggestions

- Use a `1 × 1` grid containing `#` and expect `Yes` (PRE-1–PRE-3, POST-1–POST-3).
- Use a single row `#?#` and expect `Yes`. Replace `?` with `.` and expect `No` (POST-1–POST-3).
- Use a `3 × 3` grid with black cells at opposite corners and white at the center. Expect `No` because any rectangle containing both black cells contains the white cell (POST-1–POST-2).
- Use a `1000 × 1000` grid with black cells at opposite corners and every other cell unpainted. Expect `Yes` because the rectangle can cover the entire grid (PRE-1, POST-1–POST-3).
- Use a single row `?#?`, which admits several valid completions, and expect one `Yes` line (POST-1, POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

- Behavior for input that violates PRE-1, PRE-2, or PRE-3.
